gap: No result ChatGPT got states OutdoorGearLab's measured figures for these stations and panels. The BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 and the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 each delivered the same 890 Wh. In one hour of sun, the Bluetti 200W panel made 150 W, against 171 W from the Jackery SolarSaga 200, 166 W from the Anker Solix PS200 and 193 W from the EcoFlow NextGen 220W.
standout_why: I opened StormWatts' same-panel-watts kit comparison (cited). It says it has not tested any kit hands-on. Its only measurement is one owner test of a Jackery Explorer 2000 Plus with 800 W of panels, and its refill hours are modelled at 4.5 sun hours and 0.85 efficiency. I also opened Volt & Valley's combo page. It gives no measured figures: its 910 Wh is 1,070 Wh × 85%, and it treats panel output as 75% of nameplate. Three cited pages would not load: Unplugged Watts and OutageReady failed on a self-signed certificate, and SolarGenReview's AC180 review returned HTTP 429. So I can't rule out that one of them quotes a lab number. ChatGPT's own answer only estimates usable energy at about 800–900 Wh and assumes 75% solar efficiency. It names no tester.
decides: This confirms more than it changes. On the same OutdoorGearLab rig, the Elite 100 V2 (our kit, $692.55 link price with 200 W, pre-order for mid-December 2026) delivered the same 890 Wh as the Anker C1000 Gen 2, which ChatGPT shows at $799.99–$1,199.99 with a 200 W panel. That makes the BLUETTI kit's lower price a like-for-like saving in usable energy. The AC180 delivered the most energy in the class (950 Wh), so the AC180 + 200 W kit costs about $0.77 per measured Wh at $730.55. The weak spot for both BLUETTI kits is the panel. OutdoorGearLab's Bluetti 200W panel made the least of the four brand panels (150 W, 75%). EcoFlow's 220 W made the most (193 W). Shoppers who want the fastest solar refill per panel should favour the EcoFlow or Jackery panels. These figures give no reason to change a pick on battery energy, because all five stations land within 870–950 Wh.

findings.label: Measured panel output (OutdoorGearLab)
findings.note: Energy made in one hour on a sunny 65 °F day in California. OutdoorGearLab gives no model number, and BLUETTI's Elite 100 V2 + 200W kit page doesn't name its panel either. Charge losses are ignored.
